To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) intentional forgetting contributes to mental health by allowing us to approach new experiences unencumbered by negative emotions and memories of previous negative events, (b) the intention to forget affects consolidation and thus the ease of subsequent retrieval of the to-be-remember or to-be-forgotten information, and (c) the intention to remember can have unintended side effects, such as the dampening of hippocampally encoded memories.
(a) forgetting is a dynamic process, (b) forgetting is a process, (c) the process is modulated by intention and context, and (d) the outcome is not always as intended.
the intention to suppress memory can have unintended consequences on the memory system and that the intention to direct forgetting can be limited in its scope.
